research_conclusion: Momentum (long the previous 5-day return, hold 1 day, daily rebalance) is the first candidate signal class of this research series that is NOT falsified: it earns a REGIME_STABLE positive edge in 7/10 of the collected large-cap universe with uniformly positive walk-forward segment medians (e.g. AAPL [+0.071, +0.054, +0.092, +0.069], TSLA [+0.132, +0.016, +0.107], AMZN [+0.065, +0.076, +0.077]) and low dispersion across volatility blocks; 2/10 assets (JNJ, XOM) are CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE (small positive medians at the noise threshold); 1/10 (JPM) is REGIME_DEPENDENT. This directly contradicts the a-priori falsification prediction (that momentum would mirror reversal's uniformly-negative results) and is instead internally consistent with the documented short-horizon momentum anomaly: the reversal class (short the previous return) was uniformly negative everywhere, momentum (long the previous return) is uniformly positive. The result was independently verified via a fresh walk_forward recomputation (MATCH on all per-asset and universe medians and verdicts) and determinism was asserted; the framework's warmup+train equity compounding understates (never fakes) the edge, making the finding conservative. The synthetic perturbation sweep baseline matches the null, but this is expected — the synthetic generator (regime-switching GBM with no return autocorrelation) contains no momentum structure, so the sweep validates tooling rather than testing momentum robustness. The momentum frontier cell closes as SUPPORTED; admission of momentum to the trusted evidence base is pending further scrutiny (cross-sectional momentum, longer horizons, or a broader universe) rather than being dismissed, and the framework verdict machinery continues to label this correctly as REGIME_STABLE (uniformly positive) rather than REGIME_STABLE_LOSS (which is reserved for uniformly negative results).
